verdictStatement: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. The central equality test passes twice over: the named fourteen is == equal to live G09 v3's namedCorpusNotAuthored and == equal to live g09-named-corpus-catalog.v1's, and the catalog's own class ids are the same fourteen in the same order. A stronger cross-check also holds — v5's summary.leftoverDesign is == identical to live G09 v3's leftoverDesignRemainingOnDR105, the same eight obligations in the same order — so the join's leftover set reconstructs the harness specification's exactly. R-10 and R-6 are not folded in: neither token appears among the fourteen, both remain separate obligations at leftoverDesign true, and the G09 v3 sentence the join quotes to justify the separation is character-exact, which I confirmed by locating the key nested under whatThisCloses after a top-level lookup returned nothing. OBL-FX-NAMED-CATALOG carries leftoverDesign false in specifiedNotLeftover, scoped to the naming claim only and disclosing the catalog's CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds-NOTHING standing rather than implying a recording. No FX identifier is invented — the only non-live FX tokens are fragments of the two OBL- obligation names, verified by prefix on every occurrence. Every cited digest matches with zero mismatches across thirteen basedOn pairs and sixteen recordedInputs, recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head and live HEAD with the superseded commit kept under an explicitly historical key, the D-163 recorded predecessor is still pinned alongside the successor chain, leftover-design is not claimed closed, nothing is SATISFIED, required-now is 26, no DR-G* row is added, and the subject did not move. Four further refutations of my own — a misattributed quotation, an overstated catalog standing, displacement of the recorded predecessor, and a smuggled D9 or envelope — all failed against live bytes.
